233 AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/DivRepChartRange.lean

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivRepAffPullClause

/-!
# U2 as an equation between morphisms: the chart maps lie in the range of the classifier

`Picard/DivRepAffPullClause.lean` reduced the whole divisor-representability chain to a
single hypothesis, `DivRepChartFamily.IsChartClause U`, and `IsChartClause.of_id` showed
that its `ω`-quantifier collapses to the identity point, i.e. to the DDR9-U ε-identity as
`informal/w4-ddr9-worksheet.md` §3.1 states it.  That is still a *submodule* identity with
a `∀`-quantifier over tower tests and framings hidden inside `IsDivRepClassify`.

This file removes that quantifier.  The backward classifier `divRepClassifyZar`
(`Picard/DivRepClassifyZar.lean`) is defined for **every** locally certified class over
**every** affine test, unconditionally, and `isDivRepClassify_unique` says it is the
*only* morphism satisfying the clause.  So the clause is not an extra property at all:

> `IsDivRepClassify F₀ v` ↔ `(divRepClassifyZar … F₀).left = v`.

Both directions are one line — forward is uniqueness, backward is a rewrite — and the
consequence is that U2 becomes an **equation between two morphisms of schemes that both
already exist**:

> U2 ↔ for each pair chart `(i, j)`, `(divRepClassifyZar … (U i j)).left = ChartMap i j`.

Reading off the existential, the last obligation of divisor representability is that
each chart map lies in the **range** of the classifier at its own chart ring:

> `divFunctor_representableBy_of_chartRange` :
>   `(∀ i j, ∃ F, (divRepClassifyZar … F).left = ChartMap i j) →`
>   `(divFunctor C π g).RepresentableBy DivOver`

Since `divRepClassifyZar` is injective on classes (`eq_of_isDivRepClassify`,
`Picard/DivRepClassifyZarSep.lean`), representability of `divFunctor` is *equivalent* to
surjectivity of `divRepClassifyZar` at every affine test; what this file records is that
surjectivity at the **chart rings alone** suffices.  That is the honest content: the
classifier is already a bijection onto its range everywhere, and the whole remaining debt
is that the finitely many chart points are hit.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.isDivRepClassify_iff_divRepClassifyZar_left_eq` — the clause **is**
  the classifier equation, in both directions.  General: no chart family, no universal
  point.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivRepChartFamily.isChartClause_iff_forall_classify_eq` — U2 as a
  per-chart equation of morphisms, **as an iff**, so it is a reduction and not merely a
  restatement (the safeguard of inbox `I-0571`).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.divFunctor_representableBy_of_chartRange` — divisor
  representability from range membership of the chart maps.

## What this does NOT do

It produces no class over a chart ring, so it clears no gate: U2 is unproved and, per
roadmap `…divrep.u2`, the production of a chart class with the tautological ε remains the
G-4 obligation.  What changes is what a producer has to exhibit — a class whose classifier
*is* the chart map, rather than a family satisfying a quantified submodule identity.  The
endpoint also still carries `hO`, `hχ` and the ambient curve instances.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option quotPrecheck false
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

open Grassmannian Scheme

section Curve

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))}
variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite pi]

noncomputable local instance instOverCleftDivRepChartRange :
    C.left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) := ⟨C.hom⟩

variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
  [IsIntegral C.left]
  [LocallyOfFiniteType (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
  [QuasiCompact (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
  [IsDominant pi]
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
variable [Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 0)]
  [Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1)]
variable (hpi : pi ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
variable (g : ℕ)
variable (hO : Sheaf.h0 (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1)
variable (hchi : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
variable (r1 r2 : ℕ)
variable (b1 : Module.Basis (Fin r1) k
  ↥(divisorSections k (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤))
variable (b2 : Module.Basis (Fin r2) k
  ↥(divisorSections k
    ((windowM_choice pi hpi g + windowS_choice pi hpi g) • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤))

local notation "DivOver" =>
  divSchemeOver k (windowS_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi)
    (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) g r1 r2 b1
    (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm)

local notation "ChartRing" => fun i j =>
  DivCarveChartRing k (windowS_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi)
    (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) g r1 r2 b1
    (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm) i j

local notation "ChartMap" => fun i j =>
  divCarveChartToDivScheme k (windowS_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi)
    (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) g r1 r2 b1
    (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm) i j

/-! ## `Spec` of an identity algebra map -/

/-! ## `Spec` of an identity algebra map -/

/-- `Spec` of the identity `k`-algebra map is the identity morphism.

Stated for an abstract algebra `A` on purpose.  At `A := DivCarveChartRing …` the same
step inside a tactic block does not elaborate: the rewrite pattern of
`AlgHom.id_toRingHom` is stated through the `RingHom` coercion, and matching it against
the chart ring's `Ideal.Quotient` type forces the elaborator to unfold the quotient while
`glueData`'s `ULift` index is still being unified (recorded hazard).  Abstracting the
algebra keeps the rewrite at the level where the named lemmas apply. -/
theorem specMap_ofHom_algHom_id (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] :
    Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (AlgHom.id k A).toRingHom)
      = CategoryStruct.id (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) := by
  have hid : (AlgHom.id k A).toRingHom = RingHom.id A := rfl
  rw [hid, CommRingCat.ofHom_id, Spec.map_id]

/-! ## The clause is the classifier equation -/

include hO hchi in
/-- **`IsDivRepClassify` is an equation, not a property.**  The backward classifier
`divRepClassifyZar` is defined for every locally certified class over every affine test,
and `isDivRepClassify_unique` makes it the *unique* morphism satisfying the characterizing
clause.  So a morphism satisfies the clause for `F₀` exactly when it **is** the classifier
of `F₀`.

Forward is uniqueness against `divRepClassifyZar_isDivRepClassify`; backward is a rewrite.
Mentioning no chart family and no universal point, this is what turns the DDR9-U
ε-identity into an equation between two already-existing morphisms of schemes (see
`DivRepChartFamily.isChartClause_iff_forall_classify_eq`). -/
theorem isDivRepClassify_iff_divRepClassifyZar_left_eq {S : Type u} [CommRing S]
    [Algebra k S] (F₀ : DivFamZar C S pi g)
    (v : Spec (CommRingCat.of S) ⟶
      DivScheme k (windowS_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi)
        (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) g r1 r2 b1
        (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm)) :
    IsDivRepClassify hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 F₀ v ↔
      (divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 S F₀).left = v := by
  refine ⟨fun hv => ?_, fun hv => ?_⟩
  · exact isDivRepClassify_unique hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 F₀
      (divRepClassifyZar_isDivRepClassify hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 F₀) hv
  · rw [← hv]
    exact divRepClassifyZar_isDivRepClassify hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 F₀

/-! ## U2 as a per-chart equation of morphisms -/

namespace DivRepChartFamily

set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000 in
-- Both directions instantiate `IsDivRepClassify` at the chart ring, whose `DivCarveChartRing`
-- quotient type the elaborator unfolds while unifying `divRepPullAt`'s `mapAlgHom`; the same
-- defeq profile as `IsChartClause.of_id`, which is budgeted identically.
include hO hchi in
/-- **U2, as an equation between morphisms** — and an **iff**, so it is a reduction of the
obligation rather than a restatement of it (the safeguard of inbox `I-0571`).

`IsChartClause U` holds exactly when, for each pair chart `(i, j)`, the backward
classifier of the supplied chart class *is* that chart's own map to `DivScheme`.  The
`ω`-quantifier collapses by `IsChartClause.of_id`, and the clause at the identity point is
the classifier equation by `isDivRepClassify_iff_divRepClassifyZar_left_eq`.

So the DDR9-U ε-identity carries no residual quantifier over tower tests or framings: what
a producer owes is that two morphisms `Spec R_Z(i,j) ⟶ DivScheme g`, both of which already
exist unconditionally, agree. -/
theorem isChartClause_iff_forall_classify_eq
    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
      DivFamZar C (ChartRing i j) pi g) :
    IsChartClause (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U ↔
      ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
        (divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 (ChartRing i j) (U i j)).left
          = ChartMap i j := by
  refine ⟨fun hU i j => ?_, fun hU => IsChartClause.of_id hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 fun i j => ?_⟩
  · -- instantiate the clause at the identity point of the chart
    have h := hU (S := ChartRing i j) i j (AlgHom.id k (ChartRing i j))
    rw [divRepPullAt_id] at h
    -- `Spec` of the identity algebra map is the identity; the rewrite is done at an
    -- ABSTRACT algebra (`specMap_ofHom_algHom_id`) because the same step spelled inline
    -- against the chart ring's quotient type does not elaborate.
    rw [specMap_ofHom_algHom_id (k := k), Category.id_comp] at h
    exact (isDivRepClassify_iff_divRepClassifyZar_left_eq hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2
      (U i j) (ChartMap i j)).mp h
  · exact (isDivRepClassify_iff_divRepClassifyZar_left_eq hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2
      (U i j) (ChartMap i j)).mpr (hU i j)

end DivRepChartFamily

/-! ## Representability from range membership -/

include hO hchi in
/-- **Divisor representability from range membership of the chart maps** — the form this
file exists to state.

`divRepClassifyZar` is injective on classes (`eq_of_isDivRepClassify`), so representability
of `divFunctor` is *equivalent* to the classifier being surjective at every affine test.
This says surjectivity at the **chart rings alone** suffices: if each chart map
`ChartMap i j` is the classifier of *some* locally certified class over its own chart ring
`R_Z(i,j)`, then `divFunctor C π g` is represented by `divSchemeOver`.

Nothing here produces such a class; per roadmap `…divrep.u2` that is the G-4 obligation.
The value is the shape of what is owed: a *preimage under a landed map*, at
`glueData`-many points, rather than a quantified submodule identity. -/
noncomputable def divFunctor_representableBy_of_chartRange
    (hrange : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
      ∃ F : DivFamZar C (ChartRing i j) pi g,
        (divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 (ChartRing i j) F).left
          = ChartMap i j) :
    (divFunctor C pi g).RepresentableBy DivOver :=
  divFunctor_representableBy_of_chartClause hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2
    (fun i j => (hrange i j).choose)
    ((DivRepChartFamily.isChartClause_iff_forall_classify_eq hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2
      (fun i j => (hrange i j).choose)).mpr (fun i j => (hrange i j).choose_spec))

end Curve

end AlgebraicGeometry

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartUnivReduce

/-!
# DAT-B B-6: the local-surjectivity half of the `(f, hf)` handoff

`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` (`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) needs two things beyond the
charts: the `hf` certificate (C9b, reduced in `Picard/Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean`) and the
instance

```
[Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]
```

which is dat-b row B-6.  Three files carry that instance as a `variable`
(`JacobianDataCharts.lean:117`, `JacobianDataAbelSurj.lean:183`,
`JacobianDataAbelImage.lean:131`) and **nothing anywhere produces one**.  This file supplies
the producer, in the form that DAT-B's coverage statement can actually feed.

## What local surjectivity unfolds to, and why that matters here

Mathlib's `Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective J f` has a single field: for every object `T` and
every section `s` of the target at `T`, the *image sieve* of `s` — the sieve of maps
`g : T' ⟶ T` along which `s` pulls back into the image of `f` — is a covering sieve.

For the Zariski topology on schemes that is exactly the geometric statement dat-b row B-5
proves: **every degree-zero class on a test is, locally on that test, a chart value**.  So
B-6 is not a further geometric obligation on top of B-5 — it is B-5 phrased against
mathlib's sieve-theoretic interface, plus the bookkeeping that turns a family of charts into
`Sigma.desc`.

The bookkeeping is what this file provides, and it is not trivial: the section must be hit
by *some* chart of the family, and `Sigma.desc` must be shown to see it.  That is
`ChartsCoverLocally` below.

## The honest scope, stated up front

`ChartsCoverLocally` is the hypothesis, not a theorem.  Its content is B-5 and B-5's residue
is recorded on the dat-b roadmap row (the chart-parameter/threshold reconciliation).  What
this file establishes is that **nothing else** stands between B-5 and the instance the
producer needs — in particular no compatibility across charts, because `Sigma.desc` has
none to check.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.ChartsCoverLocally` — the coverage hypothesis, stated exactly as the
  image sieve of `Sigma.desc` being covering, but spelled in terms of the individual charts
  so a producer never has to reason about the coproduct.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc` — **B-6**: that hypothesis gives the
  instance `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartsCoverLocally_of_forall_surjective` — the degenerate sufficient
  condition (a chart that is surjective on points of every test already covers), recorded so
  the hypothesis is visibly *satisfiable* and not a disguised falsehood.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

noncomputable section

variable (C) in
/-- **The coverage hypothesis of DAT-B, stated per chart rather than on the coproduct.**

For every test `T` and every degree-zero class `s` on it, the maps into `T` along which `s`
becomes the value of *some* chart of the family form a Zariski covering sieve.

This is dat-b row B-5 verbatim — "every `pic⁰` point is Zariski-locally a chart point" — with
one deliberate design choice: the sieve is described through the individual `f i`, so a
producer discharges it by exhibiting, for each point of `T`, one open neighbourhood and one
index.  It never has to mention `Sigma.desc` or the coproduct of yoneda presheaves.  Turning
that into the coproduct form is `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc` below. -/
def ChartsCoverLocally {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) : Prop :=
  ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)),
    (⨆ i, Presheaf.imageSieve (f i) s) ∈ Scheme.zariskiTopology T

/-- **B-6**: the coverage hypothesis gives the local-surjectivity instance that
`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes.

The proof is the bookkeeping the row's name hides: the image sieve of `Sigma.desc f` contains
the image sieve of every individual `f i` — because a `T'`-point of `X i` gives a `T'`-point
of the coproduct through `Sigma.ι` — hence contains their supremum, and a sieve containing a
covering sieve is covering.

Note what is *not* needed: no compatibility between charts, and no injectivity.  `Sigma.desc`
imposes no coherence condition across indices (the observation `Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree.lean`
makes for `hf`, here again for coverage), so a heterogeneous atlas is admissible for B-6 on
exactly the same footing as a homogeneous one. -/
theorem isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
    (h : ChartsCoverLocally C f) :
    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f) where
  imageSieve_mem {T} s := by
    refine Scheme.zariskiTopology.superset_covering ?_ (h T s)
    refine iSup_le fun i => ?_
    rintro T' g ⟨t, ht⟩
    -- transport the witness along `Sigma.ι` and use `Sigma.ι_desc`
    refine ⟨(Sigma.ι (fun j => yoneda.obj (X j)) i).app (op T') t, ?_⟩
    rw [← ht, ← NatTrans.comp_app_apply, Sigma.ι_desc f i]

/-- **The hypothesis is satisfiable, checked rather than assumed.**

If one chart of the family is surjective on the points of every test, the coverage hypothesis
holds — its image sieve is already the maximal sieve.  This is the degenerate case (and not
the geometric situation: no single Abel chart is surjective on all tests), but it rules out
the failure mode where a `Prop`-valued hypothesis turns out to be unsatisfiable and the
"reduction" above is therefore vacuous.

Compare the two-sided check in `Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean`: there the question was whether the
datum was too *weak*; here it is whether it is too *strong*. -/
theorem chartsCoverLocally_of_forall_surjective {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (i : ι)
    (hi : ∀ T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ, Function.Surjective ((f i).app T)) :
    ChartsCoverLocally C f := by
  intro T s
  refine Scheme.zariskiTopology.superset_covering ?_
    (Scheme.zariskiTopology.top_mem T)
  intro T' g _
  exact le_iSup (fun j => Presheaf.imageSieve (f j) s) i g (hi (op T') _)

end

end AlgebraicGeometry

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartLocalSurjectivity

/-!
# DAT-B B-5: from pointwise coverage to the sieve condition

`Picard/Pic0ChartLocalSurjectivity.lean` reduced B-6 to `ChartsCoverLocally`, whose statement
is *sieve-theoretic*: for every test `T` and every degree-zero class `s` on it, the supremum
of the per-chart image sieves is a Zariski covering sieve.  The dat-b row calls that "B-5
verbatim" and says a producer discharges it "by exhibiting one open neighbourhood and one
index per point of `T`".

**That last sentence was a claim about a bridge nobody had written.**  What B-5's geometry
produces is pointwise: for each point `t` of the test, an open `W ∋ t`, an index `i`, and a
chart point over `W` whose class restricts to `s`.  What `ChartsCoverLocally` asks for is
membership of a Grothendieck topology.  The two are connected by a *cover construction* —
`Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers` at the family `{W t}` indexed by the points of `T` — and the
connection is what this file supplies.

## Why the bridge is not bookkeeping the producer can inline

Three things have to line up, and each is a place a lane would stall:

* the cover must be indexed by a type in the right universe.  Indexing by the points of `T`
  works (`↥T : Type u` for `T : Scheme.{u}`) and is the *only* index available before any
  geometry is known — a producer that tries to index by a chosen finite subcover needs
  quasi-compactness, which no row assumes;
* `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff` asks for `Presieve.ofArrows 𝒰.X 𝒰.f ≤ S.arrows`, i.e. a
  statement about the *presieve generated by the cover maps*, so the per-point witness has to
  be produced after destructing `ofArrows` — which binds the point, not an arbitrary map into
  `T`.  This is where the pointwise data is consumed;
* the per-point index makes the target sieve a *supremum*, and `le_iSup` is what turns "some
  chart works at `t`" into "the supremum contains `W t`".  Nothing forces one index to work
  at every point, which is the chart-parameter heterogeneity the dat-b row records — here it
  costs literally nothing, because `iSup` is what the statement already had.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise` — **the bridge**, stated for an
  arbitrary family of sieves: pointwise opens with a per-point index give the supremum sieve
  covering status.  No presheaf, no chart, no `pic⁰`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` — `ChartsCoverLocally` from exactly the
  data B-5 produces: per test point, an open neighbourhood, an index, and a chart point over
  that open with the right class.  **This is what a coverage lane owes, and nothing more.**
* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise` — the composite: pointwise
  coverage gives the local-surjectivity instance `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes, i.e.
  B-5 ⟹ B-6 in one step.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally` — the **converse**, and the reason this
  is a reduction rather than a restatement: the sieve condition gives back an open cover of
  the test on each of whose members some chart hits `s`.  So the pointwise form is not a
  strengthening chosen to be provable.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

noncomputable section

/-! ## The bridge, with no chart content

Stated for an arbitrary family of sieves on an arbitrary scheme, because that is all it uses:
the coverage half of B-5 is a statement about the *site*, and mixing it with the presheaf
statement is what made it look gated. -/

/-- **Pointwise data gives a covering supremum sieve.**

If every point `t` of `T` has an open neighbourhood `W t` and an index `idx t` such that the
inclusion `(W t).ι` lies in the `idx t`-th sieve, then the supremum of the family is a
Zariski covering sieve of `T`.

The proof is the cover `{W t}_{t : ↥T}` — jointly surjective because `t ∈ W t`, open
immersions because they are opens inclusions — fed to `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff`, and
then `le_iSup` at the index of the destructed point.

Note there is **no compatibility condition between different points**: `idx` is an arbitrary
function.  That is why chart-parameter heterogeneity (dat-b row, `Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree`)
costs nothing here — a supremum sieve never asks its members to agree. -/
theorem mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {T : Scheme.{u}}
    (Sv : ι → Sieve T) (W : ↥T → T.Opens) (hW : ∀ t, t ∈ W t) (idx : ↥T → ι)
    (hmem : ∀ t, (Sv (idx t)).arrows (W t).ι) :
    (⨆ i, Sv i) ∈ Scheme.zariskiTopology T := by
  refine Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mpr
    ⟨Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers (↥T) (fun t => (W t : Scheme.{u})) (fun t => (W t).ι)
      (fun t => ⟨t, ⟨t, hW t⟩, rfl⟩) (fun t => inferInstance), ?_⟩
  rintro V g ⟨t⟩
  exact le_iSup Sv (idx t) _ (hmem t)

/-! ## `ChartsCoverLocally` from what B-5 actually produces -/

variable (C) in
/-- **THE B-5 PACKAGING**: `ChartsCoverLocally` from pointwise coverage.

The hypothesis is exactly the shape the coverage geometry delivers, and is worth reading
field by field against `w4-datb` §1.2.  For every test `T`, every degree-zero class `s` on
it, and every point `t` of `T`:

* `W` — an open neighbourhood of `t`.  In the intended instantiation this is
  `chartLocusOpens` (`Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean`), whose openness is CHART-U(b) and is
  unconditional since `IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` was discharged;
* `i` — the chart index, chosen *at `t`*.  Per-point by construction, which is what the
  I-0204 non-uniformity of the twist exponent `m` requires;
* `x` — a point of the `i`-th chart scheme over `W`, i.e. the divisor family the coverage
  argument produces at the splitting field of `κ(t)`;
* `hx` — that its class is `s` restricted to `W`.

Given that, the sieve condition holds.  So a coverage lane never has to mention `Sigma.desc`,
a coproduct of yoneda presheaves, a covering sieve, or a Grothendieck topology: it produces
four things at a point and this lemma does the rest.

**What this does not do.**  It does not produce the pointwise data — that is B-5's geometry
and its residue (the chart-parameter/threshold reconciliation) is recorded on the dat-b row.
It removes the site-theoretic layer between that geometry and B-6, which had never been
written down and which the row described as though it were already there. -/
theorem chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
    ChartsCoverLocally C f := by
  intro T s
  choose W hW i x hx using h T s
  exact mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise _ W hW i fun t => ⟨x t, hx t⟩

variable (C) in
/-- **B-5 ⟹ B-6 in one step**: pointwise coverage gives the local-surjectivity instance.

The composite of `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` with `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc`.
Recorded because it is the statement a lane closing coverage wants to cite: the *only*
remaining input to the `[Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]`
instance that three files carry as an unproduced `variable` is the pointwise data above. -/
theorem isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f) :=
  isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc f (chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise C f h)

/-! ## The converse: the pointwise form is not a strengthening

A reduction whose hypothesis is strictly stronger than its conclusion is a weakening in
disguise, and the memory `reduction-needs-its-converse` is about exactly this failure.  Here
the converse holds — modulo the one difference that is genuinely there and is named. -/

variable (C) in
/-- **`ChartsCoverLocally` gives back an open cover on whose members a chart hits `s`.**

The converse direction, and the check that the pointwise hypothesis above is the right one.
From the sieve condition one extracts a Zariski cover of `T` by `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff`
and reads the supremum membership at each cover map.

**The one honest difference**, and it is why this is stated with a general `Y ⟶ T` rather than
an open of `T`: `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff` returns a cover by *arbitrary* schemes with
open-immersion maps, not by opens of `T`.  Those are the same up to isomorphism
(`Scheme.Hom.isoOpensRange`) but not on the nose, so the converse produces a cover map where
the hypothesis consumed an opens inclusion.  For the purpose this serves — showing the
pointwise data is *available*, hence not a hypothesis chosen for provability — a cover map is
exactly as good, and pretending otherwise would need a transport that adds nothing. -/
theorem pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
    (h : ChartsCoverLocally C f) (T : Scheme.{u})
    (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) :
    ∃ (𝒰 : T.Cover.{u} (Scheme.precoverage @IsOpenImmersion)),
      ∀ j : 𝒰.I₀, ∃ (i : ι) (x : 𝒰.X j ⟶ X i),
        (f i).app (op (𝒰.X j)) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (𝒰.f j).op s := by
  obtain ⟨𝒰, hle⟩ := Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mp (h T s)
  refine ⟨𝒰, fun j => ?_⟩
  have hj := hle (𝒰.X j) (𝒰.f j) (Presieve.ofArrows.mk j)
  rw [iSup, Sieve.sSup_apply] at hj
  obtain ⟨S, ⟨i, rfl⟩, x, hx⟩ := hj
  exact ⟨i, x, hx⟩

end

end AlgebraicGeometry

     9	# DAT-B B-5: from pointwise coverage to the sieve condition
    10	
    11	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocalSurjectivity.lean` reduced B-6 to `ChartsCoverLocally`, whose statement
    12	is *sieve-theoretic*: for every test `T` and every degree-zero class `s` on it, the supremum
    13	of the per-chart image sieves is a Zariski covering sieve.  The dat-b row calls that "B-5
    14	verbatim" and says a producer discharges it "by exhibiting one open neighbourhood and one
    15	index per point of `T`".
    16	
    17	**That last sentence was a claim about a bridge nobody had written.**  What B-5's geometry
    18	produces is pointwise: for each point `t` of the test, an open `W ∋ t`, an index `i`, and a
    19	chart point over `W` whose class restricts to `s`.  What `ChartsCoverLocally` asks for is
    20	membership of a Grothendieck topology.  The two are connected by a *cover construction* —
    21	`Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers` at the family `{W t}` indexed by the points of `T` — and the
    22	connection is what this file supplies.
    23	
    24	## Why the bridge is not bookkeeping the producer can inline
    25	
    26	Three things have to line up, and each is a place a lane would stall:
    27	
    28	* the cover must be indexed by a type in the right universe.  Indexing by the points of `T`
    29	  works (`↥T : Type u` for `T : Scheme.{u}`) and is the *only* index available before any
    30	  geometry is known — a producer that tries to index by a chosen finite subcover needs
    31	  quasi-compactness, which no row assumes;
    32	* `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff` asks for `Presieve.ofArrows 𝒰.X 𝒰.f ≤ S.arrows`, i.e. a
    33	  statement about the *presieve generated by the cover maps*, so the per-point witness has to
    34	  be produced after destructing `ofArrows` — which binds the point, not an arbitrary map into
    35	  `T`.  This is where the pointwise data is consumed;
    36	* the per-point index makes the target sieve a *supremum*, and `le_iSup` is what turns "some
    37	  chart works at `t`" into "the supremum contains `W t`".  Nothing forces one index to work
    38	  at every point, which is the chart-parameter heterogeneity the dat-b row records — here it
    39	  costs literally nothing, because `iSup` is what the statement already had.
    40	
    41	## Main declarations
    42	
    43	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise` — **the bridge**, stated for an
    44	  arbitrary family of sieves: pointwise opens with a per-point index give the supremum sieve
    45	  covering status.  No presheaf, no chart, no `pic⁰`.
    46	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` — `ChartsCoverLocally` from exactly the
    47	  data B-5 produces: per test point, an open neighbourhood, an index, and a chart point over
    48	  that open with the right class.  **This is what a coverage lane owes, and nothing more.**

    51	  B-5 ⟹ B-6 in one step.
    52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally` — the **converse**, and the reason this
    53	  is a reduction rather than a restatement: the sieve condition gives back an open cover of
    54	  the test on each of whose members some chart hits `s`.  So the pointwise form is not a
    55	  strengthening chosen to be provable.

    72	
    73	/-! ## The bridge, with no chart content
    74	
    75	Stated for an arbitrary family of sieves on an arbitrary scheme, because that is all it uses:
    76	the coverage half of B-5 is a statement about the *site*, and mixing it with the presheaf
    77	statement is what made it look gated. -/
    78	
    79	/-- **Pointwise data gives a covering supremum sieve.**
    80	
    81	If every point `t` of `T` has an open neighbourhood `W t` and an index `idx t` such that the
    82	inclusion `(W t).ι` lies in the `idx t`-th sieve, then the supremum of the family is a
    83	Zariski covering sieve of `T`.
    84	
    85	The proof is the cover `{W t}_{t : ↥T}` — jointly surjective because `t ∈ W t`, open
    86	immersions because they are opens inclusions — fed to `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff`, and
    87	then `le_iSup` at the index of the destructed point.
    88	
    89	Note there is **no compatibility condition between different points**: `idx` is an arbitrary
    90	function.  That is why chart-parameter heterogeneity (dat-b row, `Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree`)
    91	costs nothing here — a supremum sieve never asks its members to agree. -/
    92	theorem mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {T : Scheme.{u}}
    93	    (Sv : ι → Sieve T) (W : ↥T → T.Opens) (hW : ∀ t, t ∈ W t) (idx : ↥T → ι)
    94	    (hmem : ∀ t, (Sv (idx t)).arrows (W t).ι) :
    95	    (⨆ i, Sv i) ∈ Scheme.zariskiTopology T := by
    96	  refine Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mpr
    97	    ⟨Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers (↥T) (fun t => (W t : Scheme.{u})) (fun t => (W t).ι)
    98	      (fun t => ⟨t, ⟨t, hW t⟩, rfl⟩) (fun t => inferInstance), ?_⟩
    99	  rintro V g ⟨t⟩
   100	  exact le_iSup Sv (idx t) _ (hmem t)
   101	
   102	/-! ## `ChartsCoverLocally` from what B-5 actually produces -/
   103	
   104	variable (C) in
   105	/-- **THE B-5 PACKAGING**: `ChartsCoverLocally` from pointwise coverage.
   106	
   107	The hypothesis is exactly the shape the coverage geometry delivers, and is worth reading
   108	field by field against `w4-datb` §1.2.  For every test `T`, every degree-zero class `s` on
   109	it, and every point `t` of `T`:
   110	
   111	* `W` — an open neighbourhood of `t`.  In the intended instantiation this is
   112	  `chartLocusOpens` (`Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean`), whose openness is CHART-U(b) and is
   113	  unconditional since `IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` was discharged;
   114	* `i` — the chart index, chosen *at `t`*.  Per-point by construction, which is what the
   115	  I-0204 non-uniformity of the twist exponent `m` requires;
   116	* `x` — a point of the `i`-th chart scheme over `W`, i.e. the divisor family the coverage
   117	  argument produces at the splitting field of `κ(t)`;
   118	* `hx` — that its class is `s` restricted to `W`.
   119	
   120	Given that, the sieve condition holds.  So a coverage lane never has to mention `Sigma.desc`,
   121	a coproduct of yoneda presheaves, a covering sieve, or a Grothendieck topology: it produces
   122	four things at a point and this lemma does the rest.
   123	
   124	**What this does not do.**  It does not produce the pointwise data — that is B-5's geometry
   125	and its residue (the chart-parameter/threshold reconciliation) is recorded on the dat-b row.
   126	It removes the site-theoretic layer between that geometry and B-6, which had never been
   127	written down and which the row described as though it were already there. -/
   128	theorem chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
   129	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
   130	    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
   131	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
   132	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
   133	    ChartsCoverLocally C f := by
   134	  intro T s
   135	  choose W hW i x hx using h T s
   136	  exact mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise _ W hW i fun t => ⟨x t, hx t⟩
   137	
   138	variable (C) in
   139	/-- **B-5 ⟹ B-6 in one step**: pointwise coverage gives the local-surjectivity instance.
   140	
   141	The composite of `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` with `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc`.
   142	Recorded because it is the statement a lane closing coverage wants to cite: the *only*
   143	remaining input to the `[Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]`
   144	instance that three files carry as an unproduced `variable` is the pointwise data above. -/
   145	theorem isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
   146	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
   147	    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
   148	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
   149	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
   150	    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f) :=
   151	  isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc f (chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise C f h)
   152	
   153	/-! ## The converse: the pointwise form is not a strengthening
   154	
   155	A reduction whose hypothesis is strictly stronger than its conclusion is a weakening in
   156	disguise, and the memory `reduction-needs-its-converse` is about exactly this failure.  Here
   157	the converse holds — modulo the one difference that is genuinely there and is named. -/
   158	
   159	variable (C) in
   160	/-- **`ChartsCoverLocally` gives back an open cover on whose members a chart hits `s`.**
   161	
   162	The converse direction, and the check that the pointwise hypothesis above is the right one.
   163	From the sieve condition one extracts a Zariski cover of `T` by `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff`
   164	and reads the supremum membership at each cover map.
   165	
   166	**The one honest difference**, and it is why this is stated with a general `Y ⟶ T` rather than
   167	an open of `T`: `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff` returns a cover by *arbitrary* schemes with
   168	open-immersion maps, not by opens of `T`.  Those are the same up to isomorphism
   169	(`Scheme.Hom.isoOpensRange`) but not on the nose, so the converse produces a cover map where
   170	the hypothesis consumed an opens inclusion.  For the purpose this serves — showing the
   171	pointwise data is *available*, hence not a hypothesis chosen for provability — a cover map is
   172	exactly as good, and pretending otherwise would need a transport that adds nothing. -/
   173	theorem pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
   174	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
   175	    (h : ChartsCoverLocally C f) (T : Scheme.{u})
   176	    (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) :
   177	    ∃ (𝒰 : T.Cover.{u} (Scheme.precoverage @IsOpenImmersion)),
   178	      ∀ j : 𝒰.I₀, ∃ (i : ι) (x : 𝒰.X j ⟶ X i),
   179	        (f i).app (op (𝒰.X j)) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (𝒰.f j).op s := by
   180	  obtain ⟨𝒰, hle⟩ := Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mp (h T s)
   181	  refine ⟨𝒰, fun j => ?_⟩
   182	  have hj := hle (𝒰.X j) (𝒰.f j) (Presieve.ofArrows.mk j)
   183	  rw [iSup, Sieve.sSup_apply] at hj
   184	  obtain ⟨S, ⟨i, rfl⟩, x, hx⟩ := hj
   185	  exact ⟨i, x, hx⟩

   187	end

/-! ## Coverage without the drop -/

variable (C) in
/-- **COVERAGE, DROP-FREE** — `w4-datb` §1.2 with steps 4, 5 and 6 deleted rather than
discharged.

For a point `t` of an arbitrary test `T` and a plus class `lam`: given a finite separable
`L/κ(t)` presenting the fibre class by `M₀`, and **any** divisor `W` of the twisted class over
`L` with `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(W))`, the point `t` lies in `chartLocus C m Z lam`.

Compare `mem_chartLocus_of_drop`, whose membership half this strictly generalises: that theorem
additionally takes `g`, `e`, `hχ`, `hdeg` and a four-part point oracle, and uses none of them
for the membership conclusion.  Dropping them is what removes step 6's feedback — the drop's
output `Σ` was the only reason two different `Z`s were in play. -/
theorem mem_chartLocus_of_witness_h1 {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) (t : T.left)
    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra (Over.testPointField t) L]
    [IsScalarTower k (Over.testPointField t) L]
    [Module.Finite (Over.testPointField t) L]
    [Algebra.IsSeparable (Over.testPointField t) L]
    (M₀ : (relCurve C L).CechPic)
    (hM₀ : PicEtAff.map C L
        (picEtAffineEquiv C (Over.testPointField t) (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) lam))
      = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M₀))
    (W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor)
    (hW : Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W
      = M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) (chartTwistClass C m Z))
    (h1 : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) 1)) :
    t ∈ chartLocus C m Z lam :=
  mem_chartLocus_of_isSplitWitness_fibre C m Z lam t
    (isSplitWitness_of_witness_twistClass C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) lam) m Z M₀ hM₀
      W hW h1)

/-! ## Producing the witness from a degree threshold -/

variable (C) in
/-- **Coverage from a vanishing threshold at the splitting field.**  The theorem is TRUE and
correctly proved; the paragraph that described `hb` as "DAT-0a's threshold, so the twist exponent
is *derived*" was WRONG and is retracted below.

`hb`: every divisor of degree `≥ b` on `C_L` has vanishing `H¹`.  `hdeg`: the twisted presenting
class has `classDeg = b`, which `classDeg_presenting_twist`
(`Pic0ChartCoverageDegreeStep2.lean`) computes as `m·d₁ − deg_k Z` for a degree-zero `lam`.
Every divisor of the class has that degree (`classDeg_picClass`), so the threshold applies to the
representative `exists_picClass_eq` produces, and `mem_chartLocus_of_witness_h1` finishes.  No
effectivity is needed anywhere, which is why no drop appears.

**RETRACTED 2026-07-29 (I-0660; adjudicated in `Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack.lean`).**  The
claim that `hdeg` is "*supplied*, not assumed, once the chart index is fixed", i.e. that `b` may
be taken to be DAT-0a's bound, is FALSE at the parameter that matters:

* at a chart index legal at parameter `n` (`deg_k Z = m·d₁ − n`, which
  `chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup` requires) `hdeg` **forces `b = n`** — it determines `b` rather
  than accepting it (`ledger_forces_b_eq_n`);
* at `n = g`, `hb` at `b = g` forces **every** degree-`g` divisor to have `h⁰ = 1`
  (`hb_forces_h0_eq_one`), which is false on a curve with a moving degree-`g` family.  DAT-0a's
  own bound is `n₁·deg F + g` with `0 < deg F`, i.e. strictly above `g` for `n₁ ≥ 1`.

What survives: `hdeg` is not unsatisfiable — for any `b ≥ 0` a legal index at parameter `b.toNat`
satisfies it by construction (`index_of_threshold`), since `n` is free throughout the chart layer.
So this theorem is usable, and the residue of B-5 step 3 is the reconciliation of the chart
parameter with the threshold, not an instantiation of DAT-0a. -/
theorem mem_chartLocus_of_vanishing_bound {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T)
    (t : T.left) (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra (Over.testPointField t) L]
    [IsScalarTower k (Over.testPointField t) L]
    [Module.Finite (Over.testPointField t) L]
    [Algebra.IsSeparable (Over.testPointField t) L]
    (M₀ : (relCurve C L).CechPic)
    (hM₀ : PicEtAff.map C L
        (picEtAffineEquiv C (Over.testPointField t) (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) lam))
      = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M₀))
    -- The `classDeg L` of `hdeg` is applied to a `relCurve`-spelled class, and the
    -- `BaseChangeInstances` pack is keyed to the PRODUCT spelling `(C ⊗ overSpec k L).left`,
    -- so these three do not synthesise in the STATEMENT (a `haveI` in the proof is too late).
    -- They are not new assumptions: `instIsIntegralBaseChange`,
    -- `instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange` and `instQuasiCompactBaseChange` discharge
    -- them at every instantiation, and the proof below re-derives the rest of the pack.
    [IsIntegral (relCurve C L)]
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L))]
    [QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L))]
    [Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 0)]
    [Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 1)]
    (b : ℤ)
    (hb : ∀ D : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor,
      b ≤ Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L D →
        Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L D) 1))
    (hdeg : classDeg L (M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L)
      (chartTwistClass C m Z)) = b) :
    t ∈ chartLocus C m Z lam := by
  -- The instance pack of `BaseChangeInstances` is keyed to the PRODUCT spelling
  -- `(C ⊗ overSpec k L).left`, not to the `relCurve` alias, so the `relCurve`-spelled
  -- binders of `exists_picClass_eq` / `classDeg_picClass` do not synthesise without these
  -- re-keyings (the same pack `Pic0ChartCoverageFibre.lean:130` needs).  The `hdeg`/`M₀`
  -- binders are therefore stated in the PRODUCT spelling, so that the statement itself needs
  -- no re-keying — `relCurveMap C k L` is `(C ◁ overSpecMap (ofId k L)).left`
  -- (`relCurveMap_eq_overSpecMap_ofId`), which is also the spelling
  -- `classDeg_presenting_twist` delivers.
  haveI : IsIntegral (relCurve C L) := instIsIntegralBaseChange C L
  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) :=
    instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C L
  haveI : QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) :=
    instQuasiCompactBaseChange C L
  haveI : Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 0) :=
    instModuleFiniteHModuleZeroBaseChange C L
  haveI : Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 1) :=
    instModuleFiniteHModuleOneBaseChange C L
  obtain ⟨W, hW⟩ := Scheme.CurveDivisor.exists_picClass_eq L
    (M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) (chartTwistClass C m Z))
  refine mem_chartLocus_of_witness_h1 C lam t m Z M₀ hM₀ W hW (hb W ?_)
  rw [show Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L W
      = classDeg L (Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W) from (classDeg_picClass L W).symm,
    hW, hdeg]

variable (C) in
/-- **The coverage statement in `∃`-form**, i.e. `w4-datb` §1.2's target shape at a fixed chart
index: at a point whose splitting is known and whose twisted class hits the threshold, there is
a chart the point belongs to.

Trivial given the previous theorem; recorded because it is the shape the DAT-B B-6 packaging
(`IsLocallySurjective`) consumes, and because keeping it separate makes visible that the only
`∃` coverage still owes is over the *index*, not over any witness or drop. -/
theorem exists_mem_chartLocus_of_vanishing_bound {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T)
    (t : T.left) (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra (Over.testPointField t) L]
    [IsScalarTower k (Over.testPointField t) L]
    [Module.Finite (Over.testPointField t) L]
    [Algebra.IsSeparable (Over.testPointField t) L]
    (M₀ : (relCurve C L).CechPic)
    (hM₀ : PicEtAff.map C L
        (picEtAffineEquiv C (Over.testPointField t) (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) lam))
      = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M₀))
    -- The `classDeg L` of `hdeg` is applied to a `relCurve`-spelled class, and the
    -- `BaseChangeInstances` pack is keyed to the PRODUCT spelling `(C ⊗ overSpec k L).left`,
    -- so these three do not synthesise in the STATEMENT (a `haveI` in the proof is too late).
    -- They are not new assumptions: `instIsIntegralBaseChange`,
    -- `instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange` and `instQuasiCompactBaseChange` discharge
    -- them at every instantiation, and the proof below re-derives the rest of the pack.
    [IsIntegral (relCurve C L)]
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L))]
    [QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L))]
    [Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 0)]
    [Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 1)]
    (b : ℤ)
    (hb : ∀ D : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor,
      b ≤ Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L D →
        Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L D) 1))
    (hdeg : classDeg L (M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L)
      (chartTwistClass C m Z)) = b) :
    ∃ m' : ℕ, ∃ Z' : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor, t ∈ chartLocus C m' Z' lam :=
  ⟨m, Z, mem_chartLocus_of_vanishing_bound C lam t m Z M₀ hM₀ b hb hdeg⟩

end

89	  obtain ⟨m, g, hg, hG⟩ := hd
90	  refine ⟨m, g, hg, fun i => ?_⟩
91	  haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i))) :=
92	    isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away (g i)) (g i)
93	  obtain ⟨G, hGdiv⟩ := hG i
94	  exact ⟨G, hGdiv.trans
95	    (Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i)))
96	      h _ _)⟩
97	
98	/-- **A global certificate is a local one** (the trivial cover `g = ![1]`): the
99	certified part over `Localization.Away (1 : R)` is `mapAlg` of the family, whose
100	equations are the pulled system on the nose (`pulledEquations` IS the pullback along
101	the comparison; the regularity proofs are proof-irrelevant). -/
102	theorem CertifiedDivisorFamily.isLocallyCertified {n : ℕ}
103	    (F : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n) : IsLocallyCertified C R π n F.eqns := by
104	  refine ⟨1, fun _ => (1 : R), ?_, fun i => ?_⟩
105	  · have hrange : Set.range (fun _ : Fin 1 => (1 : R)) = {1} := Set.range_const
106	    rw [hrange, Ideal.span_singleton_one]
107	  · haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (1 : R))) :=
108	      isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away (1 : R)) 1
109	    exact ⟨F.mapAlg (Localization.Away (1 : R)) n,
110	      Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_refl _⟩
111	
112	/-! ## The mapAlg-hreg engine -/
113	
114	section MapAlgHreg
115	
116	variable {n : ℕ} {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
117	variable (R' : Type u) [CommRing R'] [Algebra k R'] [Algebra R R'] [IsScalarTower k R R']
118	
119	/-- **The mapAlg-hreg engine** (S5b): a locally certified system has regular pulled
120	equations along the comparison of an ARBITRARY test tower `R → R'`. Regularity is
121	germ-local on the curve: the charts `Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i))` cover
122	`relCurve C R'` by open immersions; over each, the composite comparison factors
123	through the certified chart `Localization.Away (g i)`, where the certificate's
124	pullback regularity (`DivisorAdaptation.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors`)
125	transports through the recorded `DivEq`. -/
126	theorem IsLocallyCertified.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors
127	    (hloc : IsLocallyCertified C R π n d)
128	    (y z : relCurve C R') (hz : z ∈ (d.cover.pullback (relCurveMap C R R')).opens y) :
129	    ((relCurve C R').presheaf.germ ((d.cover.pullback (relCurveMap C R R')).opens y)
130	        z hz).hom (Scheme.LocalEquations.pullbackEqn (relCurveMap C R R') d y)
131	      ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C R').presheaf.stalk z) := by
132	  classical
133	  obtain ⟨m, g, hg, hG⟩ := hloc
134	  -- the away charts of `R'` at the pushed cover, and their immersions
135	  haveI himm : ∀ i : ULift.{u} (Fin m),
136	      IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R'
137	        (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down)))) := fun i =>
138	    isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R'
139	      (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))) (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))
140	  -- the pushed family spans the unit ideal of `R'`
141	  have hspan' : Ideal.span (Set.range
142	      (fun i : ULift.{u} (Fin m) => algebraMap R R' (g i.down))) = ⊤ := by
143	    have hrange : Set.range (fun i : ULift.{u} (Fin m) => algebraMap R R' (g i.down))
144	        = algebraMap R R' '' Set.range g := by
145	      ext x
146	      constructor
147	      · rintro ⟨i, rfl⟩
148	        exact ⟨g i.down, ⟨i.down, rfl⟩, rfl⟩
149	      · rintro ⟨-, ⟨j, rfl⟩, rfl⟩
150	        exact ⟨⟨j⟩, rfl⟩
151	    rw [hrange, ← Ideal.map_span, hg, Ideal.map_top]
152	  refine Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_immersion_cover
153	    (fun i : ULift.{u} (Fin m) => relCurveMap C R'
154	      (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))))
155	    (fun y' => exists_relCurveMap_base_eq C R'
156	      (fun i : ULift.{u} (Fin m) => algebraMap R R' (g i.down))
157	      (fun i => Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))) hspan' y')
158	    (relCurveMap C R R') d (fun i ζ => ?_) y z hz
159	  -- over the chart at `g i`: factor the composite through the certified localization
160	  obtain ⟨G, hGdiv⟩ := hG i.down
161	  haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i.down))) :=
162	    isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away (g i.down)) (g i.down)
163	  -- the away map `Localization.Away (g i) → Localization.Away (φ (g i))` as an
164	  -- algebra tower
165	  letI : Algebra (Localization.Away (g i.down))
166	      (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))) :=
167	    (IsLocalization.map (M := Submonoid.powers (g i.down))
168	      (T := Submonoid.powers (algebraMap R R' (g i.down)))
169	      (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))) (algebraMap R R')

216	/-! ## The locally certified divisor-functor value -/
217	
218	variable (C R π)
219	variable (n : ℕ)
220	
221	/-- The divisor-equality setoid on locally certified systems (Addendum 2's mirror of
222	`divFamSetoid`): the underlying local-equation systems cut the same divisor; the local
223	certificates are per-representative data and do not enter the relation. -/
224	def divFamZarSetoid : Setoid {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations //
225	    IsLocallyCertified C R π n d} where
226	  r d₁ d₂ := Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq d₁.1 d₂.1
227	  iseqv :=
228	    ⟨fun d => Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_refl d.1,
229	     fun h => h.symm, fun h h' => h.trans h'⟩
230	
231	/-- **The locally certified divisor-functor value on the affine test `R`**
232	(`informal/spec-dd-2.md`, Addendum 2): locally certified local-equation systems of
233	degree `n` up to divisor equality. This is the carrier on which the divisor functor is
234	a Zariski sheaf — the globally certified `DivFam` remains the building block. -/
235	def DivFamZar : Type u := Quotient (divFamZarSetoid C R π n)
236	
237	namespace DivFamZar
238	
239	variable {C R π n}
240	
241	/-- The class of a locally certified system. -/
242	def mk (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) (hd : IsLocallyCertified C R π n d) :
243	    DivFamZar C R π n :=
244	  Quotient.mk (divFamZarSetoid C R π n) ⟨d, hd⟩
245	
246	lemma mk_eq_mk_iff {d₁ d₂ : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
247	    {h₁ : IsLocallyCertified C R π n d₁} {h₂ : IsLocallyCertified C R π n d₂} :
248	    mk d₁ h₁ = mk d₂ h₂ ↔ Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq d₁ d₂ :=
249	  Quotient.eq (r := divFamZarSetoid C R π n)
250	
251	/-- **The Picard class of a locally certified divisor class** `𝒪(D)`: well defined on
252	the quotient by `picClass_eq_of_divEq`. -/
253	noncomputable def picClass (F : DivFamZar C R π n) : (relCurve C R).CechPic :=
254	  Quotient.lift
255	    (fun d : {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations // IsLocallyCertified C R π n d} =>
256	      d.1.picClass)
257	    (fun _ _ h => Scheme.LocalEquations.picClass_eq_of_divEq h) F
258	
259	@[simp]
260	lemma picClass_mk (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations)
261	    (hd : IsLocallyCertified C R π n d) : picClass (mk d hd) = d.picClass :=
262	  rfl
263	
264	end DivFamZar
265	
266	variable {C R π n}
267	
268	/-- **The comparison from the globally certified value**: a certified family is
269	locally certified (trivial cover), and divisor equality is the relation on both
270	sides. Over a field the two notions agree; over a general base `toZar` is the
271	sheafification-of-value comparison. -/
272	def DivFam.toZar : DivFam C R π n → DivFamZar C R π n :=
273	  Quotient.lift
274	    (fun F : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n =>
275	      DivFamZar.mk F.eqns F.isLocallyCertified)
276	    (fun _ _ h => DivFamZar.mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr h)
277	
278	@[simp]
279	lemma DivFam.toZar_mk (F : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n) :
280	    (DivFam.mk F).toZar = DivFamZar.mk F.eqns F.isLocallyCertified :=
281	  rfl
282	
283	/-- The Picard class factors through `toZar`. -/
284	@[simp]
285	lemma DivFamZar.picClass_toZar (F : DivFam C R π n) :
286	    F.toZar.picClass = F.picClass := by
287	  induction F using Quotient.inductionOn with
288	  | h F => rfl
289

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartUnivReduce
     7	
     8	/-!
     9	# DAT-B B-6: the local-surjectivity half of the `(f, hf)` handoff
    10	
    11	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` (`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) needs two things beyond the
    12	charts: the `hf` certificate (C9b, reduced in `Picard/Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean`) and the
    13	instance
    14	
    15	```
    16	[Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]
    17	```
    18	
    19	which is dat-b row B-6.  Three files carry that instance as a `variable`
    20	(`JacobianDataCharts.lean:117`, `JacobianDataAbelSurj.lean:183`,
    21	`JacobianDataAbelImage.lean:131`) and **nothing anywhere produces one**.  This file supplies
    22	the producer, in the form that DAT-B's coverage statement can actually feed.
    23	
    24	## What local surjectivity unfolds to, and why that matters here
    25	
    26	Mathlib's `Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective J f` has a single field: for every object `T` and
    27	every section `s` of the target at `T`, the *image sieve* of `s` — the sieve of maps
    28	`g : T' ⟶ T` along which `s` pulls back into the image of `f` — is a covering sieve.
    29	
    30	For the Zariski topology on schemes that is exactly the geometric statement dat-b row B-5
    31	proves: **every degree-zero class on a test is, locally on that test, a chart value**.  So
    32	B-6 is not a further geometric obligation on top of B-5 — it is B-5 phrased against
    33	mathlib's sieve-theoretic interface, plus the bookkeeping that turns a family of charts into
    34	`Sigma.desc`.
    35	
    36	The bookkeeping is what this file provides, and it is not trivial: the section must be hit
    37	by *some* chart of the family, and `Sigma.desc` must be shown to see it.  That is
    38	`ChartsCoverLocally` below.
    39	
    40	## The honest scope, stated up front
    41	
    42	`ChartsCoverLocally` is the hypothesis, not a theorem.  Its content is B-5 and B-5's residue
    43	is recorded on the dat-b roadmap row (the chart-parameter/threshold reconciliation).  What
    44	this file establishes is that **nothing else** stands between B-5 and the instance the
    45	producer needs — in particular no compatibility across charts, because `Sigma.desc` has
    46	none to check.
    47	
    48	## Main declarations
    49	
    50	* `AlgebraicGeometry.ChartsCoverLocally` — the coverage hypothesis, stated exactly as the
    51	  image sieve of `Sigma.desc` being covering, but spelled in terms of the individual charts
    52	  so a producer never has to reason about the coproduct.
    53	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc` — **B-6**: that hypothesis gives the
    54	  instance `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes.
    55	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartsCoverLocally_of_forall_surjective` — the degenerate sufficient
    56	  condition (a chart that is surjective on points of every test already covers), recorded so
    57	  the hypothesis is visibly *satisfiable* and not a disguised falsehood.
    58	-/
    59	
    60	set_option autoImplicit false
    61	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    62	
    63	universe u
    64	
    65	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
    66	
    67	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    68	
    69	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    70	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    71	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    72	
    73	noncomputable section
    74	
    75	variable (C) in
    76	/-- **The coverage hypothesis of DAT-B, stated per chart rather than on the coproduct.**
    77	
    78	For every test `T` and every degree-zero class `s` on it, the maps into `T` along which `s`
    79	becomes the value of *some* chart of the family form a Zariski covering sieve.
    80	
    81	This is dat-b row B-5 verbatim — "every `pic⁰` point is Zariski-locally a chart point" — with
    82	one deliberate design choice: the sieve is described through the individual `f i`, so a
    83	producer discharges it by exhibiting, for each point of `T`, one open neighbourhood and one
    84	index.  It never has to mention `Sigma.desc` or the coproduct of yoneda presheaves.  Turning
    85	that into the coproduct form is `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc` below. -/
    86	def ChartsCoverLocally {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
    87	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) : Prop :=
    88	  ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)),
    89	    (⨆ i, Presheaf.imageSieve (f i) s) ∈ Scheme.zariskiTopology T
    90	
    91	/-- **B-6**: the coverage hypothesis gives the local-surjectivity instance that
    92	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes.
    93	
    94	The proof is the bookkeeping the row's name hides: the image sieve of `Sigma.desc f` contains
    95	the image sieve of every individual `f i` — because a `T'`-point of `X i` gives a `T'`-point
    96	of the coproduct through `Sigma.ι` — hence contains their supremum, and a sieve containing a
    97	covering sieve is covering.
    98	
    99	Note what is *not* needed: no compatibility between charts, and no injectivity.  `Sigma.desc`
   100	imposes no coherence condition across indices (the observation `Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree.lean`
   101	makes for `hf`, here again for coverage), so a heterogeneous atlas is admissible for B-6 on
   102	exactly the same footing as a homogeneous one. -/
   103	theorem isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
   104	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
   105	    (h : ChartsCoverLocally C f) :
   106	    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f) where
   107	  imageSieve_mem {T} s := by
   108	    refine Scheme.zariskiTopology.superset_covering ?_ (h T s)
   109	    refine iSup_le fun i => ?_
   110	    rintro T' g ⟨t, ht⟩
   111	    -- transport the witness along `Sigma.ι` and use `Sigma.ι_desc`
   112	    refine ⟨(Sigma.ι (fun j => yoneda.obj (X j)) i).app (op T') t, ?_⟩
   113	    rw [← ht, ← NatTrans.comp_app_apply, Sigma.ι_desc f i]
   114	
   115	/-- **The hypothesis is satisfiable, checked rather than assumed.**
   116	
   117	If one chart of the family is surjective on the points of every test, the coverage hypothesis
   118	holds — its image sieve is already the maximal sieve.  This is the degenerate case (and not
   119	the geometric situation: no single Abel chart is surjective on all tests), but it rules out
   120	the failure mode where a `Prop`-valued hypothesis turns out to be unsatisfiable and the
   121	"reduction" above is therefore vacuous.
   122	
   123	Compare the two-sided check in `Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean`: there the question was whether the
   124	datum was too *weak*; here it is whether it is too *strong*. -/
   125	theorem chartsCoverLocally_of_forall_surjective {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
   126	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (i : ι)
   127	    (hi : ∀ T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ, Function.Surjective ((f i).app T)) :
   128	    ChartsCoverLocally C f := by
   129	  intro T s
   130	  refine Scheme.zariskiTopology.superset_covering ?_
   131	    (Scheme.zariskiTopology.top_mem T)
   132	  intro T' g _
   133	  exact le_iSup (fun j => Presheaf.imageSieve (f j) s) i g (hi (op T') _)
   134	
   135	end
   136	
   137	end AlgebraicGeometry

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartPair
     7	
     8	/-!
     9	# THE ATLAS IS CHART-PARAMETER HETEROGENEOUS — each chart may carry its own `n`
    10	
    11	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack.lean` establishes that at a chart index legal at parameter
    12	`n` the coverage theorem's threshold is forced to equal `n`, and that at `n = g` the resulting
    13	hypothesis is false.  Both that file and the review it adjudicates (I-0660) then reason about
    14	"the" chart parameter, as though the atlas had one.
    15	
    16	**It does not, and this file proves it.**  `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`
    17	(`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) takes a family `f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ pic0SigmaSheaf`
    18	indexed by an arbitrary `ι`, with `X : ι → Scheme` and a *per-index* certificate
    19	`hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i)`.  Nothing ties the `X i` together, so nothing ties
    20	their chart parameters together either: `mixedParamChart` below builds such a family from a
    21	per-index parameter `nn : ι → ℕ`, a per-index representation of `divFunctor C π (nn i)`, and a
    22	per-index chart index legal *at that index's own parameter*.
    23	
    24	## Why this matters, and it changes the shape of the residue
    25	
    26	The `b = n` calibration is per-chart.  So the question "can coverage use DAT-0a's threshold?"
    27	does not have to be answered uniformly: a point whose splitting field has threshold `b_L` can be
    28	covered by *the chart whose parameter is `b_L.toNat`*, and a different point by a different
    29	chart.  The I-0204 non-uniformity of `m` — no single exponent works for every fibre — is
    30	therefore **not** an obstruction to the atlas; it is an argument for an atlas indexed by the
    31	threshold, which is what a heterogeneous family is.
    32	
    33	What this does **not** do, and the honest limit of the observation:
    34	
    35	* it does not produce the representations.  `mixedParamChart` takes `rep i` as a hypothesis, one
    36	  per parameter, and the divisor-representability lane supplies `divFunctor C π g` — a single
    37	  parameter.  So the heterogeneous atlas is *admissible* but not yet *inhabited* beyond `n = g`;
    38	* it does not discharge `IsChartUniv` at any index (still CERT-Σ-gated, `Pic0ChartPair.lean`);
    39	* it says nothing about local surjectivity, which is DAT-B B-6 and is what would actually consume
    40	  the freedom.
    41	
    42	So the correct statement of the residue, refining `Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack`'s: **B-5's step 3
    43	is a question about which parameters `divFunctor C π n` is representable at, not about
    44	reconciling one parameter with one threshold.**  If representability is available only at `n = g`
    45	then the slack must go into `Z` (and its legality is open, as recorded there); if it is available
    46	at every `n`, coverage can be assembled chart-by-chart against each fibre's own threshold and the
    47	`b = n` forcing is harmless.  That is a sharper question than either prior reading, and it is
    48	addressed to the divRep lane rather than to this one.
    49	
    50	## Main declarations
    51	
    52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mixedParamChart` — a chart family with a per-index chart parameter.
    53	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_mixedParamChart` — its `hf` clause is exactly a
    54	  per-index `IsChartUniv`, so heterogeneity costs nothing in the certificate.
    55	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mixedParamRepresentableBy` — such a family is admissible input to
    56	  `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`.  **This is the whole point**: the DAT-glue seam never sees a
    57	  chart parameter.
    58	-/
    59	
    60	set_option autoImplicit false
    61	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    62	
    63	universe u
    64	
    65	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
    66	
    67	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    68	
    69	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    70	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π]
    71	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    72	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    73	
    74	noncomputable section
    75	
    76	variable (C π) in
    77	/-- **A chart family whose chart parameter varies with the index.**
    78	
    79	Each index `i` carries its own degree parameter `nn i`, its own representing object `D i` of
    80	`divFunctor C π (nn i)`, its own twist exponent `m i` and chart index `Z i` — the latter legal
    81	*at `nn i`*, i.e. `deg_k (Z i) = (m i)·d₁ − nn i`, which is what `chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup`
    82	requires for that index's chart value to land in `pic⁰`.
    83	
    84	The construction is just `restrictChart` of `abelSigmaChart` applied pointwise; the content is
    85	that it *typechecks*, i.e. that the target `pic0SigmaSheaf C` is parameter-free. -/
    86	def mixedParamChart {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
    87	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))

401	kernel of their difference (so the `FlatCokernel` base-change keystone applies
402	verbatim); the equalizer description is `mem_gluedSubmodule_iff`. -/
403	noncomputable def gluedSubmodule : Submodule R A.chartProd :=
404	  LinearMap.ker (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight)

406	/-- The equalizer description of the glued colength module: componentwise agreement of
407	the two overlap restrictions. -/
408	lemma mem_gluedSubmodule_iff (s : A.chartProd) :
409	    s ∈ A.gluedSubmodule ↔ ∀ p : A.index × A.index,
410	      A.toOvlLeft p.1 p.2 (s p.1) = A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2 (s p.2) := by
411	  simp only [gluedSubmodule, LinearMap.mem_ker, LinearMap.sub_apply, sub_eq_zero,
412	    funext_iff, deltaLeft, deltaRight, LinearMap.pi_apply, LinearMap.coe_comp,
413	    Function.comp_apply, LinearMap.proj_apply, AlgHom.toLinearMap_apply]

415	/-- The glued colength module, as a type. -/

418	/-! ### The certificate -/
419	
420	/-- **The colength certificate** (worksheet §1.1 (c1)/(c2) in the spec-dd-1 §1c frozen
421	spelling): chart-local colengths finite projective over `R` (c1); the glued module
422	finite projective of constant fibre rank `n` — honest finrank at every prime through
423	`Module.rankAtStalk` (c2); and the two flat-cokernel clauses (c3)/(c4) that make
424	certificates base-change along ARBITRARY test maps (trivial over a field; transported
425	by right-exactness; consumed by `FlatCokernel.tensorKer_bijective_of_flat_coker`). -/
426	structure IsCertified (n : ℕ) : Prop where
427	  /-- (c1) Each chart-local colength module is a finite `R`-module. -/
428	  finite_colength : ∀ j, Module.Finite R (A.colength j)
429	  /-- (c1) Each chart-local colength module is projective over `R`. -/
430	  projective_colength : ∀ j, Module.Projective R (A.colength j)
431	  /-- (c2) The glued colength module is a finite `R`-module. -/
432	  finite_glued : Module.Finite R A.Glued
433	  /-- (c2) The glued colength module is projective over `R`. -/
434	  projective_glued : Module.Projective R A.Glued
435	  /-- (c2) The glued colength module has constant fibre rank `n`. -/
436	  rankAtStalk_glued : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, Module.rankAtStalk A.Glued p = n
437	  /-- (c3) The cokernel of `W(d) ↪ Π_j colength j` is flat. -/
438	  flat_coker_incl : Module.Flat R (A.chartProd ⧸ A.gluedSubmodule)
439	  /-- (c4) The cokernel of the difference arrow is flat. -/
440	  flat_coker_diff :
441	    Module.Flat R (A.ovlProd ⧸ LinearMap.range (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight))
442	
443	end DivisorAdaptation

445	/-! ## The certified family and the divisor-functor value -/
446	
447	variable (n : ℕ)
448	
449	/-- **A certified divisor family of degree `n` over the test ring `R`** (the worksheet's
450	(D1) pair `(d, c)`): a local-equation system with a certified finite chart
451	adaptation. -/
452	structure CertifiedDivisorFamily [IsAffineHom π] : Type u where
453	  /-- The local-equation system on the relative curve. -/
454	  eqns : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations
455	  /-- The finite chart adaptation refining it. -/
456	  adaptation : DivisorAdaptation C R π eqns
457	  /-- The colength certificate of degree `n`. -/
458	  certified : adaptation.IsCertified n
459	
460	/-- The divisor-equality setoid on certified families: the underlying local-equation
461	systems cut the same divisor (`Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq`); the adaptation and
462	certificate are per-representative data and do not enter the relation. -/
463	def divFamSetoid [IsAffineHom π] : Setoid (CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n) where
464	  r F G := Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq F.eqns G.eqns
465	  iseqv :=
466	    ⟨fun F => Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_refl F.eqns,
467	     fun h => h.symm, fun h h' => h.trans h'⟩
468	
469	/-- **The divisor-functor value on the affine test `R`** (worksheet §1.1): certified
470	divisor families of degree `n` up to divisor equality. A `Type u` quotient — the
471	carrier the affine-opens-limit vehicle ranges over. -/
472	def DivFam [IsAffineHom π] : Type u := Quotient (divFamSetoid C R π n)
473	
474	namespace DivFam
475	
476	variable {C R π n} [IsAffineHom π]
477	
478	/-- The class of a certified family. -/
479	def mk (F : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n) : DivFam C R π n :=
480	  Quotient.mk (divFamSetoid C R π n) F
481	
482	lemma mk_eq_mk_iff {F G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n} :
483	    mk F = mk G ↔ Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq F.eqns G.eqns :=
484	  Quotient.eq (r := divFamSetoid C R π n)
485	
486	/-- **The Picard class of a divisor family** `𝒪(D)`: well defined on the quotient by
487	the class laws (`picClass_eq_of_divEq`). This is the Abel hook DAT-C consumes. -/
488	noncomputable def picClass (F : DivFam C R π n) : (relCurve C R).CechPic :=
489	  Quotient.lift (fun F : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n => F.eqns.picClass)
490	    (fun _ _ h => Scheme.LocalEquations.picClass_eq_of_divEq h) F
491	
492	@[simp]
493	lemma picClass_mk (F : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n) :
494	    picClass (mk F) = F.eqns.picClass :=
495	  rfl
496	
497	end DivFam

8	/-!
9	# U2 as an equation between morphisms: the chart maps lie in the range of the classifier
10	
11	`Picard/DivRepAffPullClause.lean` reduced the whole divisor-representability chain to a
12	single hypothesis, `DivRepChartFamily.IsChartClause U`, and `IsChartClause.of_id` showed
13	that its `ω`-quantifier collapses to the identity point, i.e. to the DDR9-U ε-identity as
14	`informal/w4-ddr9-worksheet.md` §3.1 states it.  That is still a *submodule* identity with
15	a `∀`-quantifier over tower tests and framings hidden inside `IsDivRepClassify`.
16	
17	This file removes that quantifier.  The backward classifier `divRepClassifyZar`
18	(`Picard/DivRepClassifyZar.lean`) is defined for **every** locally certified class over
19	**every** affine test, unconditionally, and `isDivRepClassify_unique` says it is the
20	*only* morphism satisfying the clause.  So the clause is not an extra property at all:
21	
22	> `IsDivRepClassify F₀ v` ↔ `(divRepClassifyZar … F₀).left = v`.
23	
24	Both directions are one line — forward is uniqueness, backward is a rewrite — and the
25	consequence is that U2 becomes an **equation between two morphisms of schemes that both
26	already exist**:
27	
28	> U2 ↔ for each pair chart `(i, j)`, `(divRepClassifyZar … (U i j)).left = ChartMap i j`.
29	
30	Reading off the existential, the last obligation of divisor representability is that
31	each chart map lies in the **range** of the classifier at its own chart ring:
32	
33	> `divFunctor_representableBy_of_chartRange` :
34	>   `(∀ i j, ∃ F, (divRepClassifyZar … F).left = ChartMap i j) →`
35	>   `(divFunctor C π g).RepresentableBy DivOver`
36	
37	Since `divRepClassifyZar` is injective on classes (`eq_of_isDivRepClassify`,
38	`Picard/DivRepClassifyZarSep.lean`), representability of `divFunctor` is *equivalent* to
39	surjectivity of `divRepClassifyZar` at every affine test; what this file records is that
40	surjectivity at the **chart rings alone** suffices.  That is the honest content: the
41	classifier is already a bijection onto its range everywhere, and the whole remaining debt
42	is that the finitely many chart points are hit.
43	
44	## Main declarations
45	
46	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isDivRepClassify_iff_divRepClassifyZar_left_eq` — the clause **is**
47	  the classifier equation, in both directions.  General: no chart family, no universal
48	  point.
49	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivRepChartFamily.isChartClause_iff_forall_classify_eq` — U2 as a
50	  per-chart equation of morphisms, **as an iff**, so it is a reduction and not merely a
51	  restatement (the safeguard of inbox `I-0571`).
52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divFunctor_representableBy_of_chartRange` — divisor
53	  representability from range membership of the chart maps.
54	
55	## What this does NOT do
56	
57	It produces no class over a chart ring, so it clears no gate: U2 is unproved and, per
58	roadmap `…divrep.u2`, the production of a chart class with the tautological ε remains the
59	G-4 obligation.  What changes is what a producer has to exhibit — a class whose classifier
60	*is* the chart map, rather than a family satisfying a quantified submodule identity.  The
61	endpoint also still carries `hO`, `hχ` and the ambient curve instances.
62	-/

108	    (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm)

122	/-- `Spec` of the identity `k`-algebra map is the identity morphism.
123	
124	Stated for an abstract algebra `A` on purpose.  At `A := DivCarveChartRing …` the same
125	step inside a tactic block does not elaborate: the rewrite pattern of

130	theorem specMap_ofHom_algHom_id (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] :
131	    Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (AlgHom.id k A).toRingHom)
132	      = CategoryStruct.id (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) := by

139	/-- **`IsDivRepClassify` is an equation, not a property.**  The backward classifier
140	`divRepClassifyZar` is defined for every locally certified class over every affine test,
141	and `isDivRepClassify_unique` makes it the *unique* morphism satisfying the characterizing
142	clause.  So a morphism satisfies the clause for `F₀` exactly when it **is** the classifier

145	Forward is uniqueness against `divRepClassifyZar_isDivRepClassify`; backward is a rewrite.
146	Mentioning no chart family and no universal point, this is what turns the DDR9-U
147	ε-identity into an equation between two already-existing morphisms of schemes (see
148	`DivRepChartFamily.isChartClause_iff_forall_classify_eq`). -/
149	theorem isDivRepClassify_iff_divRepClassifyZar_left_eq {S : Type u} [CommRing S]
150	    [Algebra k S] (F₀ : DivFamZar C S pi g)
151	    (v : Spec (CommRingCat.of S) ⟶
152	      DivScheme k (windowS_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi)
153	        (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) g r1 r2 b1
154	        (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm)) :
155	    IsDivRepClassify hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 F₀ v ↔
156	      (divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 S F₀).left = v := by
157	  refine ⟨fun hv => ?_, fun hv => ?_⟩
158	  · exact isDivRepClassify_unique hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 F₀
159	      (divRepClassifyZar_isDivRepClassify hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 F₀) hv
160	  · rw [← hv]
161	    exact divRepClassifyZar_isDivRepClassify hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 F₀

165	namespace DivRepChartFamily
